title: US Or Iran, Who Violated The Washington-Tehran Ceasefire MoU? Ex-Israeli Negotiator's Big Claim
summary: Former Israeli negotiator Daniel Levy claims the United States failed to honour key elements of the interim Washington-Tehran ceasefire MoU, convincing Iran that Washington was not committed and contributing to renewed hostilities. Both countries accuse each other of breaching the deal amid disputes over sanctions, military strikes and incidents in the Strait of Hormuz.
content:
US-Iran War:The US-Iran ceasefire memorandum of understanding (MoU) has come under fresh scrutiny as both the United States and Iran accuse each other of violating its terms. US President Donald Trump first alleged that Iran had breached the agreement. Tehran later responded by accusing Washington of breaking the MoU through continued military action and renewed pressure measures.

Former Israeli negotiator Daniel Levy has now argued that the United States failed to honour several commitments under the agreement, saying this convinced Iran that Washington was not serious about implementing the deal.

The interim US-Iran memorandum signed in June began to fall apart after hostilities resumed, with both countries blaming the other for the first breach.

Iran’s foreign ministry said Washington had driven the MoU “into crisis". US officials, however, argued that Iranian attacks on shipping and other targets amounted to the first violation of the agreement.

The reported disagreement has centred on continued military strikes, renewed sanctions and disputed incidents in the Strait of Hormuz.

Iran has accused the United States of violating the MoU by continuing military strikes and reintroducing sanctions and pressure measures that it says contradicted the ceasefire agreement.

Tehran has also argued that Washington abandoned its commitments while negotiations were still underway. As a result, Iran says it has suspended its own obligations under the memorandum.

The United States, meanwhile, maintains that Iran violated the agreement first through attacks on commercial shipping and other targets.

A major point of dispute has been the Strait of Hormuz, where the memorandum included arrangements for safe passage and non-interference.

After attacks on commercial vessels resumed, both Washington and Tehran pointed to those incidents as evidence that the other side had broken the agreement first. The competing claims further weakened confidence in the ceasefire.

In practical terms, the memorandum is now being viewed as badly damaged and possibly no longer functioning, with both governments blaming each other for triggering its collapse.

Speaking on the latest episode of RT’s Going Underground, former Israeli negotiator Daniel Levy argued that the United States was unwilling to implement what it had agreed with Iran in the MoU.

“I don’t think the Americans were willing to follow through what they had agreed with Iran. They couldn’t impose it on Iran because there is a different power equation there," he said.

Levy referred to Article 5 of the memorandum, which states that, upon signing, Iran would make arrangements for the safe passage of commercial vessels through the Strait of Hormuz.

According to Levy, the United States instead insisted that vessels use a separate passageway close to the coast of Oman.

“The Americans then creating this passageway hugging the coast of Oman, insisting that vessels use that passageway. That’s not what’s in Article 5," he said.

Levy also argued that US actions between Israel and Lebanon amounted to “an abrogation of Article 1" of the memorandum.

Former Israeli Negotiator Daniel Levy details How the US🇺🇸 violated the Memorandum of Understanding with Iran:‘I don’t think the Americans were willing to follow through what they had agreed with Iran. They couldn’t impose it on Iran because there is a different power equation...…https://t.co/TWNA342AoHpic.twitter.com/AYc9IT6hIL

— Going Underground (@GUnderground_TV)July 25, 2026

He further claimed that the failure to unfreeze Iranian assets violated “Article 10 or 11". According to Levy, these developments convinced Iran that Washington was not committed to implementing the agreement and pushed both sides back into an escalating cycle.

He said there had been resistance within the US system to the memorandum that US Vice President JD Vance had taken the lead in concluding, leading to frustration and renewed attempts to increase military pressure on Iran.

Levy also claimed Israel encouraged that approach and influenced developments by presenting intelligence, “whether real or cooked". He cited reports about alleged Iranian assassination attempts against Trump and claims that centrifuges for uranium enrichment had been moved to Pickaxe Mountain.

“And so, unfortunately, in this current configuration, it comes down to one person. The unpredictability, the incoherence, the lack of strategy and the ability to pull in your direction a President Trump, even if he’s been burned already by this war, he gets pulled back to the fire," Levy said.
